entry.title: Evolving the Java Language: An Inside Perspective
entry.summary: In this JavaOne keynote, Java Language Architect Brian Goetz takes you inside the process of evolving Java. Through examples spanning lambdas, records, pattern matching, virtual threads, etc., he explores the decisions, constraints, and tradeoffs behind features that feel like they’ve always belonged.

entry.title: JavaOne 2027 & Java 28 Value Objects - Inside Java Newsletter
entry.summary: In this edition, we share content highlights from recent events featuring the Java team and take a look at Value Objects in JDK 28. With technical articles, videos, and podcasts, there’s something for everyone. But nothing beats an in-person conversation, and JavaOne 2027 is the perfect opportunity to connect with the people shaping Java’s future.

entry.title: Why It Takes 3000 Commits to Bring Valhalla’s Value Objects to the JDK
entry.summary: JEP 401 (Value Objects) arrives in OpenJDK as a preview feature, enabling a new Java type model with minimal code changes. The talk explains what value objects are, JVM benefits, Valhalla history, implementation details, and the path toward bridging objects and primitives, including future support like List<int>.

entry.title: Adaptive Heap Sizing + Numeric Conversion + Primitive Patterns - Inside Java Newscast #117
entry.summary: ZGC gets adaptive heap sizing, value classes complicate numeric conversions, and primitive patterns are withdrawn as JDK 28 takes shape.

entry.title: Announcing Oracle WebLogic Server and Coherence 26
entry.summary: Oracle is pleased to announce Oracle WebLogic Server and Coherence 26! This release brings Jakarta EE 11 support, Java SE 21 and 25 support, new application development capabilities, stronger security defaults, and improvements to data processing, persistence, and operational management.

entry.title: Withdrawing the Primitive Patterns Preview Feature
entry.summary: We have decided to cease development of Primitive Types in Patterns, instanceof, and switch. The draft JEP https://openjdk.org/jeps/8393282 that would have been the sixth preview of this feature will be withdrawn, and the feature will be removed from JDK 28.

entry.title: Java and the Next Generation of Programming Models
entry.summary: Modern software increasingly interacts with AI models, query languages, and other specialized programming models, forcing you to switch contexts, embed foreign code, or write verbose wrappers to bridge the gap. What if you could express logic from outside the JVM directly in Java? In this session, we start by looking at how Java enables you to safely interact with runtimes outside of the JVM using the Foreign Function and Memory API and tools like jextract. Then will push further with Project Babylon’s code reflection: express AI models as Java programs that Babylon can analyze, transform and lower to inference engines, thus leveraging hardware accelerator backends while skipping external model files or the need to glue code.
